clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old male with no significant past medical history presented with one month of progressively worsening headaches resistant to usual analgesics. Neurological and somatic examinations were completely normal at initial presentation. Brain MRI on admission revealed a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor with sub-falcial and temporal herniation, initially suspected to be a high-grade glial tumor. Complete surgical excision was performed, and pathological examination with immunohistochemical study confirmed grade III hemangiopericytoma according to WHO 2016 classification. Adjuvant radiotherapy using VMAT technique was administered at a total dose of 54Gy with good tolerance. Control imaging 3 months after completion of radiotherapy showed no abnormalities.
